title: About
text:
Sergio Huertas-Hernández is a tenure-track Assistant Professor at the School of Government and Public Administration, Universidad Mayor, Chile. His research sits at the intersection of comparative politics, political institutions, and legislative studies, with a regional focus on Latin America.
His work examines executive-legislative relations, oversight institutions, opposition behavior, and democratic resilience. He uses quantitative, comparative, and qualitative methods to study how institutional rules shape political incentives and outcomes.
For publications, teaching, and contact information, use the navigation links above or return to the home page.

title: Sergio Huertas-Hernández
text:
Assistant Professor (Tenure-Track)
School of Government and Public Administration, Universidad Mayor
Santiago, Chile

Email X ResearchGate Google Scholar LinkedIn Bluesky ORCID





I am a tenure-track Assistant Professor at the School of Government and Public Administration, Universidad Mayor, in Santiago, Chile. I am also an Associate Researcher at the Millennium Nucleus for the Study of Political Crises in Latin America (CRISPOL) and a Research Fellow at the V-Dem Regional Center for Latin America.
My research examines how political institutions shape the performance and resilience of democracy. I focus on executive-legislative relations, legislative oversight, opposition behavior, checks and balances, and regime change in Latin America. Across these areas, I study the incentives that guide political actors and the conditions under which representative institutions constrain - or fail to constrain - executive power.
I use a multi-method research strategy that combines quantitative analysis with comparative and qualitative evidence. My work draws on statistical modeling, game theory, Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA), archival research, and natural language processing to study legislative processes, institutional rules, and political behavior.
My research has appeared in Party Politics, Parliamentary Affairs, Political Research Quarterly, The Journal of Legislative Studies, Journal of Ethnic and Migration Studies, and PS: Political Science & Politics, among other outlets. I have also contributed to Spanish-language editions of the V-Dem Democracy Report and to research projects funded by Chile’s National Agency for Research and Development (ANID).
I hold a Ph.D. and an M.A. in Political Science from the Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile, an M.Res. in Comparative Politics from FLACSO Ecuador, and a B.A. in Political Science from Universidad del Tolima, Colombia. My doctoral dissertation, Oversight of the Executive by the Legislative Opposition in Latin America, was awarded the highest distinction.
